title: SRE SLOs, Capacity Planning, Reliability Initiatives and Runbook Standards
author: Ari Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines Redwood Inference SRE standards for Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and error budgets, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, incident review expectations, required operational tooling, and canonical runbook formats. The goal is consistent, measurable reliability across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments while providing clear operational playbooks for oncall responders and owners.

Scope: Applies to all public-facing inference services (API gateway, generation endpoints, embeddings, streaming) and internal control-plane components that affect customer availability.

1) SLO & Error Budget Policy

Summary: Every externally-facing service must have at least one SLO tied to customer-visible success criteria. SLOs are expressed as an availability or latency objective over a 30-day rolling window unless otherwise noted.

Required SLOs (examples and defaults):
- API Availability (critical path): 99.95% availability (30d rolling). Success = 2xx responses for authenticated requests.
- Model Inference Latency (generation-start): p95 < 350ms for default model-family endpoints (30d rolling).
- Embeddings Throughput / Latency: p95 < 200ms for single-input embedding requests.
- Control Plane (deploy/rollout API): 99.9% availability (30d).
- Non-critical background jobs (batch model conversions): 99% availability (30d).

Error Budget and Burn Policy:
1. Error budget = 1 - SLO. Track burn rate daily and weekly.
2. If burn rate > 2x expected over a 24h window, initiate SRE review and restrict production changes (see Change Freeze below).
3. If remaining error budget < 20% for the 30d window, require mandatory postmortem for any outage and escalate to platform leadership.
4. If remaining error budget < 10%: impose a code freeze for non-critical changes, increase monitoring cadence, and schedule mitigation work (autoscaling, fallback policies, or capacity increases).

Change Freeze Rules:
- Soft freeze at <20%: only hotfixes and critical security/availability fixes allowed; all changes require SRE approval.
- Hard freeze at <10%: only emergency fixes; all deployments must be coordinated with SRE and product.

SLO Ownership and Metadata (required for each SLO page):
- Owner: team and oncall rotation (e.g., runtime-team-oncall).
- Primary metric (PromQL / dashboard link).
- Measurement window and burn-rate thresholds.
- Error budget policy link and runbook.

2) Capacity Planning Process

Objective: Ensure service capacity meets demand with required SLO headroom and cost-efficiency. Planning cadence: quarterly capacity review + monthly spot checks.

Steps (quarterly):
1. Demand Forecasting: combine historical traffic (last 90-180 days), product roadmap signals, marketing events, and committed Dedicated capacity contracts.
2. Headroom Targets: target 40-60% spare capacity for production pools for hosted tenants at baseline. For Dedicated plans, reserve contractual throughput + 20% buffer.
3. Stress & Failure Testing: schedule at least one capacity game-day per quarter (see Game-day checklist below).
4. Procurement & Allocation: request cloud GPU instances or adjust node pools 30-45 days prior to planned need.
5. Autoscaling Policy Review: ensure autoscalers (horizontal and vertical) have sensible cooldowns, minimum replica counts, and scheduled policies for predictable traffic spikes.

Capacity Table (example requirements):
- Service: Generation API | Metric: p95 latency & throughput | Headroom: 50% spare GPU slots | Lead Owner: runtime-team
- Service: Embeddings | Metric: requests/sec | Headroom: 40% | Lead Owner: models-platform
- Service: Control Plane | Metric: request success-rate | Headroom: 30% | Lead Owner: infra-platform

Game-day checklist (minimum):
- Define success criteria and SLO targets to observe.
- Inject traffic profiles (thundering herd, gradual ramp).
- Validate autoscale, batching, and KV-cache behavior.
- Measure tail latency and token emission rates.
- Document findings and action items.

3) Reliability Initiatives (OKR-driven)

Initiatives should be measurable and owned. Typical multi-quarter initiatives:
- Reduce p99 latency of generation-start by 30% for high-traffic models.
- Implement prefix KV-cache for customers with >100 qps to reduce repeated context cost by 40%.
- Harden fallback chains to switch to next-best model-family within 500ms on capacity pressure.
- Improve end-to-end canary testing for model rollouts to detect regressions before 1% of traffic.

For each initiative include: problem statement, owner, target metric, timeline, and success criteria. Track in the SRE roadmap board and report monthly.

4) Incident Review Standards

Goal: Blameless, actionable postmortems with clear remediation and verification steps.

Postmortem template (required fields):
- Incident ID (e.g., INC-2026-0453)
- Severity (sev1 | sev2 | sev3)
- Start/End timestamps (UTC)
- Impact summary (services, customers, regions affected, estimated % of requests affected)
- Timeline of events (minute-level for sev1)
- Root cause analysis (technical and contributing human/process factors)
- Immediate mitigations performed
- Long-term remediation plan with owners and due dates
- Roll-forward verification steps and metrics to confirm fix
- Lessons learned and follow-ups (link to JIRA/epic)

Postmortem expectations:
- Draft within 48 hours for sev1, 5 business days for sev2.
- Assigned remediation owners for each action with SLAs (30/60/90 days).
- Publish to the incident-review area and present during next SRE retro.

5) Operational Tooling (required stack and configuration)

Minimum stack members:
- Metrics: Prometheus + Cortex (multi-tenant), metrics retention 90d for service dashboards.
- Tracing: Jaeger/OpenTelemetry, with 30d sampling retention for traces that meet error/latency thresholds.
- Logging & Search: ELK stack / BigQuery export for long-term storage, 365d retention for security/audit logs.
- Alerting & Oncall: PagerDuty (routing by service), with notification escalation paths and runbook links attached to each alert.
- Dashboards: Grafana per-service dashboards (SLO, latency distribution, error budget burn-rate).
- Incident Communication: Slack incident channels with predefined templates and status-page integration.

Alerting guidance:
- Alert on symptoms not thresholds alone (e.g., increase in 5xx rate, error budget burn-rate > 2x expected).
- All actionable alerts must include: symptoms, immediate mitigation steps (link to runbook), and owner contact.
- Use noise reduction: aggregation windows, deduplication rules, and dependent service suppression.

6) Runbook Standards and Template

Runbook requirements: every runbook must be concise, actionable, and tested at least annually. Include:
- Runbook ID and canonical page link
- Purpose and scope
- Symptoms that trigger this runbook
- Quick checks (metrics/queries to run)
- Immediate mitigation steps (ordered)
- Rollback / fallback steps (if applicable)
- Post-incident tasks and diagnostics to collect
- Owner and escalation contacts
- Last tested date and test owner

Canonical Runbook Example (Generation API - high latency)
- Title: generation-api-high-latency
- Symptoms: p95 generation-start > 350ms OR sustained p99 > 1s across 5m window
- Quick checks:
  1) Check Prometheus: rate(5xx) and p95 latency panel (dashboard link).
  2) Check GPU utilization and queue lengths (node exporter / agent metrics).
  3) Check KV cache hit-rate for affected model-family.
- Immediate mitigations (ordered):
  1) Scale up inference pool (increase replica count or add nodes).
  2) Switch traffic to fallback model-family via smart routing policy (pre-configured policy id).
  3) Enable reduced-batch, lower-concurrency mode for affected pool (button on console).
  4) If degradation persists, open incident channel and notify pagerduty oncall.
- Diagnostics to collect: profiler snapshot, tail logs, recent model load events, CPU/GPU telemetry.
- Owner: runtime-team-oncall; Escalation: runtime-team-lead -> eng-sre-manager

Runbook testing and maintenance:
- Each runbook must have a last-tested date and a short result summary.
- Annual tabletop exercise required for high-severity runbooks.

7) Roles & Escalations

- First responder: owning service oncall.
- SRE escalation: if mitigation cannot be implemented within 30 minutes or root cause spans multiple systems.
- Product/Customer Success escalation: for customer-impacting incidents with committed SLAs or Dedicated customers.

8) Compliance and Audit

- SLO ownership pages audited quarterly to ensure metadata and dashboards are current.
- Postmortems and remediation trackers retained for at least 3 years for compliance and internal learning.

Appendix A — Example Alert Rules

- generation_api_high_p95_latency: if p95_latency > 350ms for 5m -> severity: sev2; attach runbook generation-api-high-latency.
- api_5xx_rate_spike: if increase in 5xx rate by 3x over baseline for 3m -> severity: sev1.
- error_budget_burn_rate: if burn_rate_24h > 2 -> severity: sev2; trigger error-budget review.
